entity.title: Rule
entity.description: A single-phrase behavioral constraint or property definition attached to an entity.

rules.body: DEFINES a single property of an entity or describes the behavior of that property.
IS uniquely identified using a Rule Format.
Rule identifiers MUST NOT be reused, even if the rule is deprecated or deleted.
MUST be expressed as a single phrase.
MAY be supplemented by one or more notes to provide context or clarification.
HAS a Rule State.
Once a Rule IS in State other than Draft then it is immutable.
Once a Rule IS immutable, modifications must be introduced by superseding it with a new rule.
MAY declare `overrides` naming one inherited Rule, which the declaring Rule replaces within the inheriting Entity's effective rule set only.
Within an Entity, at most one Rule that is not Abandoned, Terminated or superseded MAY override a given inherited Rule.
A Rule that supersedes an overriding Rule MAY restate the `overrides` it takes over, otherwise the override lapses.
When the `supersedes` field of a Rule is not null, it MUST name a Rule of the same Entity.
DEFINE a single property of an Entity or the behavior of that property.
A change to an immutable Rule MUST be made by a new Rule that supersedes it.
MAY have a `clause`, a non-empty string naming the clause of an external standard that the Rule transcribes.
MAY have a `profiles` array of unique names of the profiles the Rule belongs to.
A Rule MUST NOT have a `clause` or `profiles` unless its Realm is a Standard Realm.

entity.title: Rule State
entity.description: The lifecycle state of a rule, governing its mutability and enforcement.

rules.body: A Rule MAY have a state: Draft (D), Abandoned (A), Published (P), Implemented (I), Retired (R), Terminated (T).
Each State can only be applied once to a Rule.
Draft IS the initial state.
Abandoned IS a terminal state which applies to Rules which were previously in Draft.
Published applies to Rule which have been validated but aren't yet implemented.
Implemented applies to Rule which are in force.
Retired applies to Rule which are still in force or present but must be removed.
Terminated applies to Rule which aren't in force anymore.
A Rule MUST NOT enter Implemented while the governed code is known to violate it.
Retired IS the State of a Rule that is still in force or present but is due to be removed.
A Rule MUST change state only from Draft to Published, Draft to Abandoned, Published to Implemented, Implemented to Retired, or Retired to Terminated, except as RULST-012 allows.
A Published Rule that another Rule supersedes MAY change state to Terminated.

notes.content: Published is the standard's position and may sit on violating code; Implemented means the rule is in force and the code complies with it.
Promote Draft to Published as soon as the wording is final, and Published to Implemented only once compliance and enforcement exist.
No other move is allowed: an Implemented Rule reaches Terminated only through Retired, and Abandoned and Terminated are terminal.

A Published Rule may not be edited, so a wrong text is fixed by a superseding Rule; the old Rule was never in force, so Retired, which is for a Rule still in force, does not fit, and Terminated marks it out of force.
SYNCOP-009 supersedes SYNCOP-008 while SYNCOP-008 is Published; SYNCOP-008 goes to Terminated and SYNCOP-009 can reach Implemented.
The superseded Rule moves to Terminated no earlier than the change in which its successor enters Published, and no later than the change in which its successor enters Implemented.

An override is distinct from supersession. Supersession replaces a Rule within the same Entity and obliges the superseded Rule to retire once the new one is Implemented; a child can never retire a parent Rule because inherited Rules are read-only references owned by the parent (ENT-009), and across Realms they are dependency imports (RLM-005). An override therefore leaves the parent Rule untouched: it is replaced only inside the inheriting Entity's effective rule set and keeps applying to the parent's own subject and to every other child. The supersedes and overrides fields are orthogonal and may coexist on one Rule.
A `clause` is fixed once its Rule leaves Draft, because RUL-007 makes the whole Rule immutable.
